summary:
piano-model: Magenta's Onsets and Frames is now the default piano transcription model, and Basic Pitch is the fallback (the client's 19:30 decision). Settings.transcriptionModel 'auto' | 'piano' | 'fast' is wired end to end. I also did the lead's 19:55 real-world check on the client's Liebestraum recording.
(1) VENDORED, NO NEW DEPENDENCY. src/engine/transcribe/oaf/ is imported only by the worker. It holds the mel front end, the model graph, chunking, the decoder, weight loading and the device logic, with Apache-2.0 headers on each derived file plus NOTICE and LICENSE. The graph is rebuilt with core tfjs ops, not tfjs-layers: BatchNorm is folded into the convolutions (in JS, before upload), activations are fused, and the LSTM runs as one fused WebGL shader per time step (plain ops on the CPU backend). With the same input, its outputs match Magenta.js 1.23.1 to about 1e-6, with zero decision flips. The shipped version feeds a copy of the first frame as left context instead of 0 dB zero padding: that padding made the model invent low notes at 0 s on noisy input (silence.wav gave 1-2 notes, now 0). Against Magenta.js this changes no onset decisions on 2 of 3 comparison files (1 on the third) and 0.35-0.6 % of frame decisions, through the LSTM's starting state. The input is padded to whole chunks of 64 frames (2 s; this also avoids the tfjs 3.21 WebGL shader bug) and streamed chunk by chunk, with Magenta's context frames and the LSTM state carried over. That keeps GPU memory flat and gives real per-chunk progress.
(2) MEL. The JS front end matches Magenta's preprocessAudio to 2.2e-4 dB and is 69x faster (40 ms vs 2.8 s for 24.6 s of audio). I measured the GPU route the prompt asked for. tf.signal.stft (tfjs 3.21 WebGL) failed to compile its shader on one input length; where it worked it was slower (86 ms vs 28 ms) and off by up to 0.18 dB. A matmul-DFT mel was exact (0.001 dB) but not faster (22-40 ms) and needs 17 MB of GPU memory. So the JS front end runs on every backend.
(3) CHECKPOINT. public/models/onsets-frames/ holds 16.5 MB (15.75 MiB) plus a NOTICE stating plainly that the code is Apache-2.0 and the checkpoint was released by Magenta and trained on MAESTRO (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Every tensor in uint8, as in the sandbox, flipped 1.9 % of frame decisions (max error 0.98). Keeping biases and BatchNorm statistics in float32 (+26 KB) and the frame-LSTM kernel in uint16 (+0.86 MB) brings that to 0.14 %, with onset flips at 5-6. It downloads lazily on first piano use, with byte progress inside 'loading-model' (0-0.09). It is cached in Cache Storage ('pauta-onsets-frames-v1') for offline use and kept out of the Workbox precache (globIgnores). Basic Pitch stays precached.
(4) PIPELINE. The tuning compensation from tuning.ts is applied in the same resampling pass that takes 22.05 kHz to 16 kHz. Onsets get +15 ms, velocities come from the model's velocity head (10..90 to 0.15..0.9), and the NoteEvent contract is unchanged.
(5) MODEL CHOICE. 'auto' uses the piano model when WebGL 2 with float32 rendering is available, a zero-weight copy of the network warms up (compiling every shader), and a one-chunk timing probe predicts at least 1x real time. All of this happens BEFORE the download, so slow devices never fetch the 16 MB. The verdict is remembered per GPU renderer for 30 days. Otherwise, and when offline before the first download, Basic Pitch runs. 'piano' skips the checks and still falls back on failure; 'fast' is Basic Pitch. Which model ran is exposed through job.model, getLastTranscriptionInfo() and TranscribeDetails.info. Fallback reasons: no-webgl2, slow, offline, load-failed, run-failed.
(6) NUMBERS. Realistic benchmark, ±50 ms: Basic Pitch 0.873 -> piano model 0.936. The sandbox reached 0.940 with float32 and 0.937 with uint8. Per condition: estudio 0.964, sala 0.974, desafinado 0.945, acelerado 0.970, movil 0.797. Liebestraum arpeggios 98/91 % (Basic Pitch 81/74), soft notes 87.5 % (78.9), velocity r 0.74 (0.47). Speed on the RTX 2060: 30 s of audio in 0.60 s, 50x real time (Basic Pitch 28x, Magenta sandbox 3.6x). On the tfjs CPU backend: 0.38x (Basic Pitch 0.74x). GPU textures after a job: 234-255 MiB (552 MiB with Magenta's 250-frame chunks).
(7) CLIENT RECORDING. Liebestraum No. 3, 163 s, from the first cadenza to the end. scripts/fixtures/align-reference.mjs aligns a reference MIDI to a recording. It uses chroma plus chroma-onset (DLNCO) features, a coarse subsequence DTW that also finds the transposition, a fine banded DTW, and onset refinement on the recording's own spectral flux, never on a transcription. Validated against exact truth on the realistic benchmark: median error 5 ms, p90 18 ms, 97 % within 50 ms. The reference is Bernd Krüger's piano-midi.de sequence (CC BY-SA, local only). The recording sounds exactly one semitone higher than the score: tuning offset 0.2 cents, transposition +1 found automatically. It covers reference bars 26-87, and bar 27 «Più animato con passione» starts at 0.69 s. Before -> after on the recording: F1 at ±50 ms was 0.534 with Basic Pitch and 0.602 with the piano model on Magenta's defaults; the tuned piano model reaches 0.666. At ±100 ms: 0.613 -> 0.747 -> 0.790. Tuning came from sweeps on this recording, checked against the benchmark: onset threshold 0.35 instead of 0.5 at the default sensitivity, with the 90 ms 'Nota mínima' kept as the minimum duration. Recall by register at ±100 ms (below C3 / C3-B3 / C4-B4 / C5 and up) went from 63/55/51/46 % (Basic Pitch) to 75/74/70/74 %. The client heard the low notes as diffuse: they are now found as often as the rest. I left Basic Pitch calibrated as shipped: its best setting for this recording (0.60/0.15, ±50 F1 0.572) costs about 0.05 on the benchmark.
(8) UI. One 'Modelo' row in Ajustes > Transcripción (Auto / Piano / Rápido, helper line «Piano es más preciso»), which fits at 320 px. One SOFTWARE credit. The pipeline passes the setting.
Feedback applied: 19:30 (integrate the piano model with Basic Pitch as the fallback) and 19:55 (reference, DTW alignment, comparison, tuning and re-comparison on the client recording).

public_api_notes:
TRANSCRIBE (import only from src/engine/transcribe/index.ts):
- transcribe(samples, { sensitivity, minNoteMs, model? }, onProgress?) is unchanged when called without model. model is a TranscriptionModel ('auto' default, from Settings.transcriptionModel).
- TranscribeJob gains model?: Promise<TranscriptionInfo>. It resolves once the worker has chosen, before inference, and stays pending if the job fails first. TranscriptionInfo = { requested, model: 'piano' | 'fast', backend: 'webgl' | 'cpu', fallback?: 'no-webgl2' | 'slow' | 'offline' | 'load-failed' | 'run-failed' }.
- getLastTranscriptionInfo() returns the info of the latest job, or null.
- Exported types: ActiveModel, PianoFallback, TranscriptionInfo.
- preloadModel(model = 'auto') never downloads the piano checkpoint. When the checkpoint is cached and 'auto' allows it (or model is 'piano'), it warms up the piano model; otherwise Basic Pitch, as before.
- NoteEvent contract unchanged: seconds of the samples passed, pitch 21..108, sorted. Velocity is the piano model's velocity head (Magenta 10..90 divided by 100, floor 0.15, the same floor as the Basic Pitch loudness velocities), so forte lands near 0.7 and soft accompaniment near 0.3. Durations follow the sounding note, pedal included.
- Progress stays monotonic with the same stages. 'loading-model' 0-0.09: real download bytes the first time (16.5 MB), then warm-up. 'analyzing' 0.1-0.9: one step per 2 s chunk. 'extracting-notes' 0.9-1. During long chunks the worker re-posts progress at most every 2 s, so the 90 s stall watchdog stays quiet on slow CPUs.
- Piano decoder at the default sensitivity: onset 0.35, frame 0.5, minimum duration = minNoteMs (90 ms). Sensitivity 0 / 0.5 / 1 maps to onset 0.6 / 0.35 / 0.2.
- Errors: same messages as before. Piano failures never surface: they fall back to Basic Pitch.
MODEL CHOICE (worker):
- 'auto' requires tfjs WebGL with WEBGL_VERSION 2 and float32 rendering. A zero-weight copy of the network warms up and is timed on one chunk (64 frames = 2 s of audio); at least 1x real time is required.
- The verdict is stored as device-verdict.json in the same Cache Storage, per GPU renderer, for 30 days. Measured: SwiftShader 11 s per 250-frame chunk = 0.7x -> 'slow' -> Basic Pitch, with nothing downloaded.
- A run-time failure marks the piano model broken for the session, and 'auto' then uses Basic Pitch.
- On the CPU backend 'auto' answers 'no-webgl2'. 'piano' still runs there (0.38x real time on this PC).
- Both models share one worker and one tfjs backend.
CACHE / OFFLINE:
- Cache 'pauta-onsets-frames-v1': weights_manifest.json, written last (its presence means complete), plus 4 shards.
- Older 'pauta-onsets-frames-*' caches are pruned. Bump the suffix in oaf/weights.ts whenever the files change.
- A damaged cache is re-downloaded once. A download with no bytes for 30 s is abandoned (offline -> Basic Pitch).
- Without Cache Storage (plain http, not localhost) the checkpoint is fetched each session.
TOOLS:
- check-transcription.mjs:
  - --model auto|piano|fast prints the model per fixture and in --json.
  - --sweep-piano [--onset a,b --frame x --min-dur 0,0.09 --shift 0.015 --sweep-tol 0.1] sweeps the piano decoder on cached activations.
  - --local / --local-only run test/fixtures/local/*.json references (git-ignored audio). They report F1 at ±50 and ±100 ms, P/R, recall by register (roles low <C3, mid-low C3-B3, mid-high C4-B4, high >=C5), and octave / semitone / merged errors. --dump <dir> writes the transcribed notes.
  - --perf prints tensors and GPU texture memory.
- Harness: RunOptions.model and RunOptions.tolerances; RunResult.model / fallback / byTolerance; window.__sweepPiano.
ALIGNMENT TOOL: node scripts/fixtures/align-reference.mjs --audio <rec> --midi <ref.mid> --out <truth.json> [--transpose auto|n] [--from-tick/--to-tick] [--no-refine] [--plot png]
- Output follows test/fixtures/real/*.json. Notes carry pitch as heard (transposition included), hand, role (register), bar, beat and refined. Also beats, downbeats, pedal, key (as heard), referenceKey, timeSignature and transpose, plus an alignment block (bars covered, first full bar and its time, DTW costs, refinement stats, every bar's start time).
- Beats come from the refined onsets, so they are as precise as the notes.
CLIENT RECORDING REFERENCE: test/fixtures/local/liebestraum-abydos.json, aligned from liebestraum-reference-krueger.mid (both local only).
- 1347 notes, transpose +1 (sounds in C major; written in B major from bar 27).
- Covers reference bars 26-87; first full bar 27 «Più animato con passione» at 0.69 s.
- 378 beats (quarter notes), 61 downbeats, 6/4 (the second cadenza is bars 60-61 at 12/4).
- Median tempo 165 quarter-note bpm, accelerating through the Più animato.
- 77 pedal spans from the reference.
- Regenerate with: node scripts/fixtures/align-reference.mjs --audio test/fixtures/local/liebestraum-abydos.mp3 --midi test/fixtures/local/liebestraum-reference-krueger.mid --out test/fixtures/local/liebestraum-abydos.json --name liebestraum-abydos
BUNDLE: the worker chunk is 1803.8 KiB (+24 KiB, no tfjs-layers); the engine client is 12.5 KiB. check-bundle 4/4.

requests.request: HomeScreen.tsx: call preloadModel(getSettings().transcriptionModel) instead of preloadModel(). The no-argument default is 'auto', which matches the default setting, but users who chose 'Rápido' should not warm the piano model, and 'Piano' users should get theirs warmed. It never downloads the checkpoint.

Optional, if useful: a quiet line in Processing with the model that runs ('Modelo de piano' / 'Modelo rápido', or only when it fell back). transcribe() returns job.model (resolves before inference) and getLastTranscriptionInfo() works after the job. PipelineJob would need to forward job.model. The first piano transcription on a phone may sit in 'Preparando' while 16.5 MB download; the progress is real (0-9 % of the model share).

Commit the new files listed in this report, including public/models/onsets-frames/ (four binary shards, 16.5 MB, plus manifest and NOTICE) and src/engine/transcribe/oaf/ (NOTICE and LICENSE included). NEVER commit test/fixtures/local/: it holds the client's Pixabay recording, the aligned reference and Bernd Krüger's CC BY-SA reference MIDI. It is already git-ignored.

Licensing, unchanged from audio-accuracy and stated in public/models/onsets-frames/NOTICE and docs/CREDITS.md: the Magenta code is Apache-2.0. The onsets_frames_uni checkpoint has no stated license and was trained on MAESTRO (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), and so was Basic Pitch. Get legal advice before any commercial release.

Rhythm on the client's recording: test/fixtures/local/liebestraum-abydos.json has 378 aligned beats, 61 downbeats and every bar's start time, accurate to about the note precision (median 5 ms, p90 18 ms on the benchmark validation). It also has meter (6/4; 12/4 for the second cadenza, bars 60-61), the sounding key C major (transpose +1 from B major) and pedal spans. Get the real transcriptions with node scripts/fixtures/check-transcription.mjs --local-only --model piano --dump <dir> (use --model fast for Basic Pitch). The piano model's onsets have MAE ~11 ms (32 ms frames) and a +7 ms bias on this recording, and its durations include pedal sustain.

FYI: I added the 'Modelo' row (Segmented Auto / Piano / Rápido, helper line «Piano es más preciso», ariaLabel 'Modelo de transcripción') at the top of TranscriptionGroup in SettingsScreen.tsx, and one SOFTWARE entry in credits.ts. I re-read both files right before editing and touched only those lines.

known_issues: Not measured on real phones. Measured: desktop GPU (RTX 2060, ANGLE D3D11) at 50-63x real time; software WebGL (SwiftShader), where the probe measured 0.7x and 'auto' chose Basic Pitch without downloading; and the tfjs CPU backend at 0.38x (Basic Pitch 0.74x). GPU textures after a job are 234-255 MiB. That is less than Magenta's 4-batch ~390 MB but could still be tight on low-end phones; a failure there falls back to Basic Pitch ('run-failed').

On a slow device the first 'auto' transcription pays for the zero-weight warm-up (shader compilation) plus a one-chunk probe before falling back. On SwiftShader that was 28 s of loading in total, including the Basic Pitch load. The verdict is then remembered per GPU for 30 days.

The vendored network deliberately differs from Magenta.js at the left edge: it repeats the first frame instead of letting the convolutions pad with 0 dB, which removed phantom notes at 0 s on noisy input. In the comparison this changes 0 or 1 onset decision per file and 0.35-0.6 % of frame decisions, through the LSTM state. Benchmark F1 0.936 vs 0.938 before the change, within noise.

Synthetic legacy fixtures (sox pluck synth, not piano): the piano model is below Basic Pitch there (mean 0.939 vs 0.971; scale.wav F1 0.94, one extra note; chords.wav 0.88 vs 0.93). On the FluidR3 piano fixtures it is far better (0.965 vs 0.869). silence.wav gives 0 notes with both.
Phone-speaker captures: the piano model gives octave errors when the fundamentals are cut (phone-moonlight-125: 36 octave extras); 'movil' F1 is 0.797 vs 0.791 for Basic Pitch.

Client recording: the remaining misses are re-strikes under the pedal merged into a ringing note (175) and inner notes of large chords (recall 0.61 for chords of 5 or more notes vs 0.79 for single notes). The reference is a score-faithful sequence, not this pianist's exact performance, so part of the 27 % missing recall at ±100 ms may be playing differences.

The recording sounds exactly one semitone above the score (tuning offset 0.2 cents): either transposed or sped up about 6 %. The aligner detects that; the transcription simply reports what sounds, which is correct.

Basic Pitch thresholds were left as calibrated: the setting that suits the client recording (onset 0.60 / frame 0.15, ±50 F1 0.534 -> 0.572) loses about 0.05 on the realistic benchmark. Users can still raise «Sensibilidad».
The piano model's onset timing is coarser than Basic Pitch's (32 ms frames): MAE 10.8 ms vs 5.7 ms on the benchmark, with a +7 ms bias on the real recording.
worker.ts is 404 lines (BRIEF suggests about 400) because it now hosts both model paths; the piano logic itself lives in oaf/piano.ts.

round2.summary: Round 2 (max accuracy + commercial licenses). (1) LICENSES. Onsets and Frames checkpoint: no license stated anywhere, so NOT usable commercially under the client's rule (current default; not deleted, decision pending). ByteDance high-resolution: weights CC BY 4.0, code Apache-2.0. Transkun V2: MIT, weights inside the repo. Basic Pitch: Apache-2.0, weights inside the repo. All four were trained on MAESTRO (CC BY-NC-SA): an open question for a lawyer. (2) ACCURACY, the official models in Python on the same audio, tuning compensation and metrics. Transkun is clearly best: realistic benchmark F1 0.973 (OaF 0.936, Basic Pitch 0.873, ByteDance 0.880-0.897). On the client recording: 0.716 at ±50 ms and 0.838 at ±100 ms (OaF 0.666 / 0.790, Basic Pitch 0.534 / 0.613). Recall at ±100 ms is 0.849, against a measured ceiling of about 0.86 for this recording. Re-strikes merged under the pedal fall from 175 to 35. ByteDance roughly equals OaF on the recording (±50 0.679, ±100 0.796 at onset 0.6), is below it on the benchmark (octave ghosts), and has the best timing and key-release offsets. (3) FUSION of the current models helps little (best ±50 0.681 / ±100 0.794): the remaining errors are model limits plus reference mismatch. 13.6 % of reference notes are found by no model even at its most sensitive, and 12.9 % of the notes three models agree on are absent from the reference. (4) BROWSER PORT. ByteDance's note model now runs in TF.js (src/engine/transcribe/hr/, NOT wired into the worker yet). Validated against PyTorch: max output difference 3e-5 and 0 decision flips on a segment; 23.1 MiB quantized (0.06 % frame flips). It runs at 8x real time on the RTX 2060, but its GPU texture pool reaches 1.56 GB. A converter bug was found and fixed: the model's BatchNorm2d receive momentum as eps (0.01). Transkun was NOT ported within the time box (axial transformer + semi-CRF). It is the recommended replacement for OaF; plan and effort below.

round2.api_proposal:
Nothing changes for callers today; the current default is still OaF. Proposal for the replacement model, additive and backwards compatible:
- NoteEvent stays { pitch, start, duration, velocity }. With models that regress offsets (Transkun, ByteDance), duration is the KEY-HELD time, not extended by the pedal. Basic Pitch and OaF durations follow the sounding note.
- TranscriptionInfo gains durations: 'key' | 'sounding', so score-accuracy knows which kind it gets.
- TranscribeJob gains pedal?: Promise<{ start: number; end: number }[]>: sustain-pedal spans in seconds of the samples passed, sorted, non-overlapping. It resolves [] when the model has no pedal output. ByteDance has a pedal model (not converted yet). Whether the shipped Transkun checkpoint outputs pedal events was not verified here.
- score-accuracy can then prefer model pedal over its inferred Score.pedals, and use key-held durations for articulated notation (the client's 'elongated notes' complaint).
replacement_plan: 1. Transkun (recommended: MIT, best accuracy). A TF.js port covers the conv backbone with down- and up-sampling, 6 axial-attention layers over frequency and time, RMSNorm and Fourier position embeddings, the inner-product interval scorer, the semi-CRF decoding in JS, and the velocity and refined-onset/offset heads, validated against PyTorch like this round's port. Estimate: 2-3 focused days. Alternative: ONNX export plus onnxruntime-web, about 1-1.5 days, but that adds an npm dependency and needs the lead's approval. Expected about 14 MB int8.

2. ByteDance (CC BY 4.0) as an interim. The port is done and validated. Remaining: cut GPU memory (batch GRU segments, avoid per-step tensor stacks), worker wiring with probe, cache and progress, and app measurements. Estimate: 0.5-1 day. Accuracy is about equal to OaF on real audio and below it on the synthetic benchmark; timing and offsets are better.
3. Retraining OaF from Magenta's Apache-2.0 code would need a commercially licensed piano dataset with aligned MIDI (MAESTRO is non-commercial), plus weeks of GPU training. Not recommended.

round3.summary: Transkun V2 (MIT) is now the piano model, running in the transcription worker through onnxruntime-web 1.30.0 on WebGPU. The front end, the semi-CRF Viterbi decoding and the segment stitching are reimplemented in TypeScript. On the realistic benchmark the app gets note F1 0.974 (Basic Pitch 0.871, Onsets and Frames 0.938 before). On the client's Liebestraum it gets 0.720 at +-50 ms and 0.850 at +-100 ms (Basic Pitch 0.534 / 0.613, OaF 0.67 / 0.80). Downloads: 30 MB of model plus the 27 MB ORT WebAssembly binary (fp16 weight storage, no note changed). Speed on this RTX 2060: 6.5x real time on 20 s clips and 10.4x on a 163 s piece, model loaded. Onsets and Frames, the hr/ ByteDance port and its converter are removed. The pedal API and TranscriptionInfo.durations are implemented.

final_api.import_from: src/engine/transcribe/index.ts (unchanged entry points: transcribe, startTranscription, preloadModel, getLastTranscriptionInfo, disposeTranscriber)
final_api.TranscribeJob: { promise: Promise<NoteEvent[]>; cancel(); model?: Promise<TranscriptionInfo>; pedal?: Promise<PedalSpan[]> }. pedal resolves together with the notes: sustain-pedal spans {start, end} in seconds of the input samples, sorted by start, from Transkun's sustain events (symbol -64). It is [] when Basic Pitch ran. It never rejects, and stays pending if the job fails or is cancelled.
final_api.PedalSpan: exported from index.ts: { start: number; end: number } (seconds).
final_api.TranscriptionInfo: { requested: 'auto'|'piano'|'fast'; model: 'piano'|'fast'; backend: 'webgpu'|'wasm'|'webgl'|'cpu'; durations: 'key'|'sounding'; fallback?: PianoFallback }. backend is where the model that ran ran: 'webgpu' for the piano model, the tfjs backend for Basic Pitch. durations: 'key' = NoteEvent.duration is the key-held time (piano model; the pedal comes separately), 'sounding' = until the note stops sounding (Basic Pitch).
final_api.PianoFallback: 'no-webgpu' (no non-fallback WebGPU adapter: phones without WebGPU, Firefox/Safari without it, SwiftShader) | 'no-webgl2' (auto only: the tfjs speed probe needs WebGL) | 'slow' (auto only: probe predicts < 1x real time) | 'offline' (files not cached and no network) | 'load-failed' | 'run-failed' | 'no-notes' (the piano model found nothing, e.g. not a piano or synthetic tones; Basic Pitch ran instead, which is [] on silence).
final_api.modes: 'auto' = piano model when WebGPU + WebGL2 + probe >= 1x, else Basic Pitch. 'piano' = piano model whenever WebGPU works (skips the probe), else Basic Pitch with the reason. 'fast' = Basic Pitch. Settings.minNoteMs / sensitivity only affect Basic Pitch now (the piano model keeps every note: no minimum duration).
final_api.note_for_score_readability: With durations 'key', note lengths are key-held times. On the client's Liebestraum the median is 0.099 s; 21 % of notes are under 50 ms and 44 % under 90 ms (benchmark median 0.456 s, 1.4 % under 50 ms). The score builder's default ScoreParams.minDuration 0.05 (src/engine/score/build.ts) would drop about a fifth of the notes of that recording. Do not filter by duration when info.durations === 'key'. Apply TranscribeJob.pedal to extend sounding lengths for playback and for the pedal marks.
